title: Smaller, Younger, and More Visible? AI-Assisted Writing, Scientific Team Composition, and the Visibility of Scientific Knowledge
abstract: arXiv:2605.27404v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Generative AI is reshaping scholarly communication, yet little is known about how AI-assisted writing relates to the organization and visibility of scientific knowledge production. This study examines the associations between AI-modified text, publication-team characteristics, and scholarly visibility. Drawing on 144,930 full-text articles and reviews from the PLoS family and the Nature Portfolio published between 2020 and 2025, we use a novel text-based detection approach to estimate AI usage scores as indirect indicators of AI-assisted writing. These scores do not directly measure actual AI use in academic writing but provide indirect signals of AI-assisted writing. We focus on two dimensions of scholarly communication: the production and dissemination of scientific knowledge. translated_title: 更小、更年轻、也更可见？AI辅助写作、科研团队构成与科学知识的可见性
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能正在重塑学术交流，然而人们对AI辅助写作与科学知识生产的组织方式及可见性之间的关系仍知之甚少。本研究考察了AI修改文本、发表团队特征与学术可见性之间的关联。基于2020至2025年间PLoS期刊家族与Nature Portfolio发表的144,930篇全文论文与综述，我们采用一种新颖的基于文本的检测方法来估计AI使用得分，作为AI辅助写作的间接指标。这些得分并不直接测度学术写作中实际的AI使用情况，而是提供AI辅助写作的间接信号。我们关注学术交流的两个维度：科学知识的生产与传播。前者体现为两项团队特征，后者则以短期引用量来衡量。我们考察了AI使用得分与……的关联（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该研究提出一种基于文本检测的AI使用得分新方法，通过分析2020–2025年间PLoS与Nature旗下14万余篇论文，揭示AI辅助写作与更小规模、更年轻的科研团队构成以及更高的短期学术可见性相关联。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a novel text-based AI usage detection approach and, drawing on 144,930 PLoS and Nature Portfolio articles published between 2020 and 2025, finds that AI-assisted writing is associated with smaller, younger research teams and greater short-term scholarly visibility.
